solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Fish Swedish chefs originally served in pastry dishes (6)

indicatorNotes.originally: originally takes the opening letter of each word
indicatorNotes.served in: the letters are served inside the dishes

blocks.note: first letters of Swedish and chefs

annotation.surface: A Scandinavian restaurant brings fish to the table in pies.
annotation.walkthrough: SC goes inside PIES, after PI. 'Fish' is plural here: Pisces is the sign of the Fishes, but the word itself also stands for fish in general.
annotation.definitionFit: Pisces is Latin for fishes and names the fish constellation and zodiac sign.

entries.clue: Quiet cleric was unwell, but gained mastery (9)

annotation.surface: A mild clergyman fell ill yet came out on top.
annotation.definitionFit: To prevail is to win out or gain the upper hand.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Quiet' reads as describing the cleric; on its own it is the musical P, piano.

entries.clue: That woman left without applying glossy coat (11)

annotation.surface: A woman departs before her nails or furniture get their varnish.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Without' looks like a subtraction instruction; here it is simply a synonym, LACKING.
annotation.definitionFit: Shellac is a resin varnish, so shellacking is putting on a glossy coat of it.

entries.clue: Guards dismissing first of such registered competitors (7)

indicatorNotes.first of: first of takes the opening letter of 'such'

blocks.note: remove S, the first letter of 'such'

annotation.surface: Security staff turning away some of the people who signed up for an event.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the sporting sense: a race's entries are the names put down to compete.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Guards' could be a verb; it is the noun, and 'first of such' names the letter to drop from it.

entries.clue: Wedding attendant married on fateful day in interwoven fabric (10)

indicatorNotes.on: in an across clue, A on B puts A after B
indicatorNotes.in: the pieces sit inside the fabric

blocks.note: braid is woven or plaited fabric
the Ides of March, the day Caesar was killed

annotation.surface: A wedding helper in a braided dress on an ill-omened date.
annotation.walkthrough: The 'fateful day' is the Ides of March, when Caesar was killed; M sits after it, and both go inside the fabric.
annotation.definitionFit: The definition is a job title for the answer: she attends the bride at the ceremony.

entries.clue: Fellow encountered in rural pharmacy (5)

indicatorNotes.encountered in: the name is met inside the next words

annotation.surface: Bumping into a man at a village chemist's.
annotation.definitionFit: Crosswords use 'fellow' for any man's name; Ralph is one.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pharmacy' seems to be where the fellow is found; it only supplies the tail of the name.

entries.clue: Study Latin with new intake, penning a factual film (11)

indicatorNotes.penning: the intake pens the A, holding it inside

blocks.note: to do a subject is to study it: 'she did French'
cum is the Latin for with
a new entry, an intake of recruits or pupils

annotation.surface: A school taking in new Latin pupils, filmed for television.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Latin with' is a translation, not an L: CUM is Latin for 'with', as in magna cum laude.
annotation.definitionFit: A documentary is a non-fiction film about real events.

entries.clue: Boss regularly met priest reforming a participant in massacre (11)

annotation.surface: A boss keeps meeting a clergyman while redeeming someone with blood on their hands.
annotation.definitionFit: Septembrists took part in the September Massacres of prisoners in Paris in 1792.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Massacre' is a real event: the September Massacres in Paris, 1792, when mobs killed prisoners during the French Revolution.

entries.clue: A northern church’s attempt to establish roots (8)

blocks.note: CE = Church of England, plus the 's

annotation.surface: A northern parish trying to plant itself in a community.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Roots' looks botanical beside 'establish'; it means family origins.
annotation.definitionFit: Your roots are your ancestry, the line you descend from.

entries.clue: Information found in sandhills on south Kent headland (9)

indicatorNotes.found in: the information sits inside the sandhills
indicatorNotes.on: in a down clue, A on B puts A below B

annotation.surface: Data gathered among the dunes of a southern English promontory.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is literally true: Dungeness is a shingle headland on the Kent coast, the county in England's south-east corner.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by location: the shingle promontory sits on the south coast of the county.

entries.clue: Engineers attack renovation of vessel, say (5)

blocks.note: RE = Royal Engineers, the British Army corps
a fit is an attack, as of coughing

annotation.surface: Army engineers assault a ship that is being overhauled.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Attack' is a noun here, a fit of illness or temper, not a military assault.
annotation.definitionFit: A refit is the overhaul of a ship; 'say' marks the ship as one example.

entries.clue: Expose girl with article in both hands (6)

indicatorNotes.in: the girl and article go inside the hands

blocks.note: R and L, right and left

annotation.surface: Exposing a girl holding an object in each hand.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to expose a secret is to bring it into view.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Both hands' means one letter for each hand, right and left, which then wrap the rest.

entries.clue: Warning to top politician — a way to get supporter on board (11)

annotation.surface: A caution to the Prime Minister about winning a backer over.
annotation.walkthrough: 'On board' suggests getting someone to agree; it means on a ship, where a mast supports the sails.
annotation.definitionFit: The foretopmast is the mast above the foremast on a sailing ship, supporting sails and rigging.

entries.clue: Heavyweight holding almost all remaining cards (5)

indicatorNotes.holding: the heavyweight holds the next piece inside

blocks.note: a ton is a great weight

annotation.surface: A card game where the big player sits on most of the pack.
annotation.definitionFit: In card games the talon is the stock of cards left after the deal.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Heavyweight' looks like a boxer; it is just a big weight, a TON.

entries.clue: Severity of poor European singers entertaining you in Paris (12)

indicatorNotes.poor: poor signals the letters are in bad shape, to be rearranged
indicatorNotes.in Paris: in Paris asks for the French word

annotation.surface: A harsh verdict on bad European singers performing for a French audience.
annotation.definitionFit: Grievousness is the quality of being grievous, that is serious or severe.
annotation.walkthrough: Only the European's E and the singers are shuffled; the French 'you' is dropped in whole.

entries.clue: English reader, a Liberal, concerned with voting (9)

blocks.note: a lector reads lessons in church, or lectures at a university

annotation.surface: An English lecturer who is a Liberal, preoccupied with elections.
annotation.definitionFit: Electoral means relating to elections and voting.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Reader' is a church or university title here: a lector reads lessons or lectures.

entries.clue: Top European is able to maintain a large missile launching site (4,9)

blocks.note: to aver is to maintain, assert

annotation.surface: A senior European official capable of running a big rocket base.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Maintain' reads as keeping something going; it is the arguing sense, to maintain that something is true.
annotation.definitionFit: Cape Canaveral in Florida is the US launch site for rockets and missiles.

entries.clue: Unsurpassed junior officer hiding in a tree (3-4)

indicatorNotes.hiding in: the officer hides inside the tree

annotation.surface: The best-ever junior officer concealed up a tree.
annotation.definitionFit: An all-time record or best has never been surpassed.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Unsurpassed' is an adjective, and so is the hyphenated answer, as in an all-time high.

entries.clue: Baskets of celebratory wine Charlie left out (7)

blocks.note: champers is British slang for champagne
Charlie = C in the phonetic alphabet; removed

annotation.surface: Gift hampers full of champagne, with Charlie missing out.
annotation.definitionFit: Hampers are lidded wicker baskets, often packed with food and drink.
annotation.walkthrough: Champers is British slang for champagne, the celebratory wine; the C of Charlie comes off its front.

entries.clue: Protein in connective tissue finally introduced to a German (7)

indicatorNotes.introduced to: LAST is introduced into the German word

annotation.surface: A German student is finally taught about a tissue protein.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Protein in connective tissue' looks as if it ends at 'tissue', and then 'finally' seems to take its last letter; 'finally' is LAST, and the whole phrase is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Elastin is the elastic protein in skin, arteries and other connective tissue.

entries.clue: Bar, merchandise and beer container — the whole lot! (4,5,3,6)

blocks.note: to bar a door is to lock it
a shop's stock is its merchandise

annotation.surface: A pub owner buying the bar, its goods and the kegs in one go.
annotation.walkthrough: The phrase really names the three parts of a gun; the clue swaps in three new meanings for them.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom from the three parts of a gun, used to mean everything, entirely.

entries.clue: King meets newsman bringing in unknown old coin (8)

indicatorNotes.bringing in: the newsman brings the unknown inside

blocks.note: Paul Julius Reuter, founder of the Reuters news agency
algebra's unknowns are x, y and z

annotation.surface: A monarch receives a journalist who has brought an unfamiliar antique coin.
annotation.definitionFit: The kreutzer was a small coin of the old German states and Austria.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Meets' just joins the king to the newsman. The newsman is the founder of the Reuters agency, and the unknown is algebra's Z.

entries.clue: Short extra box? (4)

indicatorNotes.Short: short cuts off the last letter

blocks.note: spare = extra; short means drop its last letter

annotation.surface: A question about a small spare container.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Box' reads as a noun, a container; it is the verb, to box, which is what sparring partners do.
annotation.definitionFit: To spar is to box, especially in practice; the question mark flags the verb's surprise.

entries.clue: Change form of extremely rare historical writing implement (7)

indicatorNotes.extremely: extremely takes the letters at the extremes

blocks.note: a style, or stylus, was a pointed tool for writing on wax tablets

annotation.surface: Altering the look of a very rare antique pen.
annotation.definitionFit: To restyle something is to give it a new form or look.
annotation.walkthrough: A style was the Roman stylus, pointed at one end for scratching wax tablets.

entries.clue: US politician in rally runs into moggy (8)

indicatorNotes.into: into means entering, so the runs letter enters the cat

blocks.note: a demo, or demonstration, is a protest rally
moggy is British slang for a cat

annotation.surface: An American politician at a rally collides with a stray cat.
annotation.definitionFit: A Democrat belongs to one of the two main US political parties.
annotation.walkthrough: Moggy is British slang for an ordinary cat; runs is the cricket R.

entries.clue: Tenor ultimately associated with estrangement (5)

blocks.note: a rift is a split between people

annotation.surface: A singer who, in the end, fell out with everyone.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tenor' is not the singer but the general sense of something, as in the tenor of a speech.
annotation.definitionFit: The drift of an argument is its tenor, its general meaning.

entries.clue: Stumble over young chap climbing, having three feet (8)

indicatorNotes.climbing: in a down clue, climbing reads the word upwards

blocks.note: a lad is a young chap

annotation.surface: A boy trips while scrambling up, as if he had three legs.
annotation.definitionFit: Tripodal means having three feet or legs, like a tripod.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Over' is not a positional word here but the cricket O, and 'climbing' flips the young chap upward in this down clue.

entries.clue: Plot involving girl in South Carolina port (8)

indicatorNotes.in: the girl goes in the state and port

blocks.note: Rio de Janeiro, the Brazilian port

annotation.surface: A conspiracy centred on a young woman in Charleston harbour.
annotation.walkthrough: 'South Carolina port' looks like one place, Charleston; it is the state's code followed by a Brazilian port, with the girl between.
annotation.definitionFit: A scenario is the outline plot of a play or film.

entries.clue: Beasts of burden carrying good, first-class light spears (8)

indicatorNotes.carrying: the beasts carry the letters inside

blocks.note: A1 = first-class, with the 1 read as I

annotation.surface: Pack animals loaded with fine lightweight weapons.
annotation.definitionFit: Assegais are slender spears used in southern Africa.
annotation.walkthrough: A1 means first-class, and crosswords read the 1 as the letter I.

entries.clue: Dog and donkey primarily obsessed with crested bird (8)

blocks.note: a cur is a mongrel dog

annotation.surface: A dog and a donkey fixated on a bird with a crest.
annotation.definitionFit: The curassow is a large crested game bird of tropical America.
annotation.walkthrough: Each small word counts: 'with' is the W of abbreviations like w/o.

entries.clue: Abandoned Nigel calmly, though with lack of care (11)

indicatorNotes.Abandoned: abandoned letters run wild, out of order

annotation.surface: Someone walked out on Nigel quietly but without a thought for him.
annotation.definitionFit: Negligently means carelessly, with a lack of proper care.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Abandoned' reads as leaving Nigel behind; it tells you to mix his letters up.

entries.clue: Characters in Borneo lithographing stone implement (7)

indicatorNotes.Characters in: the answer is made of letters inside the phrase

annotation.surface: Printing Bornean text onto a stone tool.
annotation.definitionFit: From Greek for 'new stone': a tool made in the New Stone Age.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Characters' looks like printing type, which suits lithographing; it just means letters, and they hide the answer.

entries.clue: Dependable NHS management — of unknown value? (11)

blocks.note: NHS hospitals in Britain are run by bodies called trusts
algebra's unknowns are x, y and z

annotation.surface: A sceptical question about how reliable health-service bosses are.
annotation.walkthrough: The NHS is Britain's National Health Service, whose hospitals are run by trusts; the question mark adds the jibe that their worth is unknown.
annotation.definitionFit: Trustworthy means dependable, able to be relied on.

entries.clue: Chitchat of abstainer in old hat, story Times breaks (6-6)

indicatorNotes.in: the abstainer goes in the hat
indicatorNotes.breaks: the Times break into the story

blocks.note: tile is old slang for a hat

annotation.surface: Gossip about a teetotaller in an outdated hat, a story broken by the Times newspaper.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Times' with its capital looks like the newspaper setting this puzzle; it is just two T's.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, a reduplicated word for idle gossip.

entries.clue: Blatancy of old boy and girl initially outraging American head (11)

blocks.note: OB = old boy, a former pupil
a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness's neighbours and Dungeness

annotation.surface: A former pupil and a girl brazenly offending an American boss.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Head' looks like a boss; it is a headland, a ness.
annotation.definitionFit: Blatancy is the quality of being glaringly obvious.

entries.clue: Noblewoman representing vet’s cousins (11)

indicatorNotes.representing: the letters are re-presented in a new order

annotation.surface: A titled lady standing in for her vet's relatives.
annotation.definitionFit: A viscountess is a noblewoman ranking below a countess.
annotation.walkthrough: Every letter of 'vet's cousins' is used; the apostrophe falls away.

entries.clue: Constrict great-aunts travelling across lake (11)

indicatorNotes.travelling: the aunts' letters travel into a new order
indicatorNotes.across: the rearranged letters lie across the lake

annotation.surface: Elderly relatives on a journey across a lake, feeling squeezed.
annotation.definitionFit: To strangulate is to constrict, cutting off flow as by squeezing.
annotation.walkthrough: The aunts' letters are shuffled and the lake's L is set among them.

entries.clue: Lacking capacity to carry table reportedly set in stone? (11)

indicatorNotes.to carry: the word for lacking capacity carries the next piece inside

blocks.note: an altar is a church table

annotation.surface: A question about an incapable altar carved in stone.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark marks 'set in stone' as a phrase for fixed, while the altar keeps the surface in a church.
annotation.definitionFit: Something set in stone is unalterable, beyond change.

entries.clue: Owned by no one — but not crazed (11)

blocks.note: possessed = crazed, as if by a demon

annotation.surface: Something without an owner, yet not out of its mind.
annotation.definitionFit: Unpossessed means not owned, and also not possessed in the demonic, frenzied sense.
annotation.walkthrough: Both readings build the same word: possessed as owned, and possessed as crazed by a demon.

entries.clue: Fellow given appointment working for advertisers (11)

blocks.note: a posting is an appointment to a job

annotation.surface: A man offered a job in an advertising agency.
annotation.definitionFit: Billposting, sticking up posters, is work done for advertisers.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Working for advertisers' looks like a description of the fellow's job; it defines the whole answer.

entries.clue: Example of popular fellow, civil engineer (8)

annotation.surface: A well-liked chap who is a model civil engineer.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: 'for example' and 'for instance' are interchangeable.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Popular' is IN, as in 'the in crowd'; 'civil engineer' is the standard CE.

entries.clue: Stop one’s free land eventually being occupied (9)

blocks.note: a colon is a punctuation stop
last letters of freE and lanD

annotation.surface: Halting a nation's free territory from being taken over.
annotation.definitionFit: A colonised country has been occupied by settlers from elsewhere.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Eventually' takes the last letter of both 'free' and 'land'.

entries.clue: Pertinent, rejecting a gang leader’s suggestion (8)

annotation.surface: A mobster's idea is relevant, so the gang turns it down.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: something put forward for consideration.
annotation.walkthrough: Apropos means pertinent; rejecting 'a' drops its first letter. Crosswords often use AL for a gangster, from Al Capone.

entries.clue: Flower starts to look inferior, nibbled by sheep (5)

indicatorNotes.starts to: starts to takes the first letters
indicatorNotes.nibbled by: the sheep bites around the letters, taking them in

blocks.note: first letters of look and inferior

annotation.surface: A bloom begins to droop after sheep chew it.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: it is one kind of flower, a spring bulb.
annotation.walkthrough: A tup is a ram, a word from northern England; 'starts to' takes one letter from each of the next two words.

entries.clue: Ruler’s earthenware vessel in French gallery (9)

blocks.note: a pot is an earthenware vessel
the Tate, the London art gallery

annotation.surface: A monarch's pottery on show in a French museum.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In French gallery' looks like the Louvre; 'in French' is EN and the gallery is London's Tate.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, usually for a monarch with absolute power.

entries.clue: Birds farm animals observed crossing barrier (8)

indicatorNotes.observed crossing: the animals are seen straddling the barrier

annotation.surface: Birds watching pigs get over a fence.
annotation.definitionFit: Swallows are fork-tailed migratory birds.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Birds' is the definition, not the ones doing the observing.

entries.clue: House acceptable for a literary pirate (4)

annotation.surface: A home that would suit a buccaneer from a novel.
annotation.definitionFit: Captain Hook is the pirate in J. M. Barrie's Peter Pan.
annotation.walkthrough: HO is a standard short form of house; OK is plain acceptable.

entries.clue: Glorify oneself — with a fanfare, perhaps? (4,4,3,7)

blocks.note: the straight sense: to boast about your own achievements
the literal picture: a fanfare is played on trumpets, so you sound your own

annotation.surface: Boasting about yourself, possibly accompanied by fanfare.
annotation.walkthrough: The idiom for boasting is read literally: someone sounding their own fanfare on a trumpet.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: to praise yourself loudly, as a herald's trumpet would.

entries.clue: Stringed instrument from our country the Spanish at last gave the French (7)

indicatorNotes.at last: at last takes the final letter

blocks.note: the UK, from a British paper's point of view

annotation.surface: Britain's Spanish residents finally hand a small guitar over to the French.
annotation.definitionFit: The ukulele (also spelt ukelele) is a small four-stringed guitar.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Our country' is the UK because the puzzle is set in The Times, a British paper; this spelling is a variant of ukulele.

entries.clue: In Berlin I invested in trains — lavishly! (6)

indicatorNotes.invested in: the German I is invested, put inside

annotation.surface: A Berliner boasts of pouring money into railways.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Invested' plays on money, which suits 'lavishly'; here it only means placed inside.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both mean in a lavish, sumptuous way.

entries.clue: Imposing building, or small one in opera? (7)

indicatorNotes.in: the small one goes in the opera

annotation.surface: A grand house, or else a tiny one on the opera stage.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for a grand, stately house.
annotation.walkthrough: Manon is Massenet's opera (Puccini's is Manon Lescaut); 'small one' is S and I.

entries.clue: Parrot beginning to make a crow’s sound (5)

indicatorNotes.beginning to: beginning to takes the first letter

annotation.surface: A parrot learning to imitate a crow.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Parrot' looks like a verb, to mimic, which fits the crow's sound; it is the bird.
annotation.definitionFit: The macaw is a large, brightly coloured parrot.

entries.clue: Most obtrusive yobbo taking in some of the French (7)

indicatorNotes.taking in: the yobbo takes the French word inside

blocks.note: a yobbo is a lout, British slang
des is French for 'some of the'

annotation.surface: The rowdiest thug welcoming a few French visitors.
annotation.definitionFit: The superlative of loud, obtrusive in the sense of noisy and hard to ignore.
annotation.walkthrough: Yobbo is British slang for a lout; DES is French for 'some of the'.

entries.clue: Container finally made for King Edward? (5)

blocks.note: last letters of madE and foR

annotation.surface: A box built especially for a king.
annotation.walkthrough: 'King Edward' looks like a monarch; it is a popular British variety of potato, and the question mark marks it as one example.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: King Edward is a British potato variety, and potatoes are tubers.

entries.clue: Time and motive for lese-majesty (7)

annotation.surface: Opportunity and motive for insulting the monarch.
annotation.definitionFit: Lese-majesty is an offence against the sovereign, a form of treason.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Time and motive' sound like a detective's checklist, which fits a crime; the two pieces simply join.

entries.clue: Old Europeans vet hols, we hear, touring capital city (13)

indicatorNotes.we hear: we hear points to what is heard, so the words are taken by their sound
indicatorNotes.touring: the sounds go around the capital

blocks.note: hols and vacs are British short forms of holidays and vacations

annotation.surface: Inspecting holiday plans for a trip around a capital.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Old' matters: Czechoslovakia split in 1993, so its citizens are former Europeans of that nation.
annotation.definitionFit: Czechoslovaks were citizens of Czechoslovakia, a European state that no longer exists.

entries.clue: Frenchman’s to go inside container to meet a dancer (9)

indicatorNotes.go inside: the French verb goes inside the container

blocks.note: aller is French for to go

annotation.surface: A Frenchman climbs into a bin to meet a dancer.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Go' works twice: 'Frenchman's to go' is the French infinitive, and 'go inside' sends it into the container.
annotation.definitionFit: The definition is general and the answer specific: a female ballet dancer.

entries.clue: Feeble wife quietly dislodged by cat (5)

indicatorNotes.dislodged by: P is dislodged, W taking its place

blocks.note: W = wife; put in P's place

annotation.surface: A timid wife nudged quietly aside by the cat.
annotation.definitionFit: Informal slang for weak or cowardly, from wuss.
annotation.walkthrough: The cat's P is taken out and the wife's W put in its place.

entries.clue: They expand a detective’s offers (10)

annotation.surface: A police detective's bids, apparently inflating.
annotation.definitionFit: Distenders are things that distend, that make something swell or expand.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Offers' is a noun, tenders as in bids for a contract, not a verb.

entries.clue: Thin and emaciated male bore (6)

blocks.note: an eagre is a tidal bore, a wave running up a river

annotation.surface: A skinny, wasted man who is also tedious company.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bore' is not a dull person but a tidal wave in a river; EAGRE is the old word for it.
annotation.definitionFit: Meagre can mean thin and lean, as of a body.
